name: clip-trimmer
title: Clip Trimmer
description: A video trimming card with a preview image, a ten-frame filmstrip and a ruler. Two orange handles set the start and end of the kept clip, dimming what gets cut, and a playhead loops over the selection.
use: A clip, recording or media file needs a quick in and out point before upload or export.
avoid: It trims numbers only, not real footage, so you must swap in your own preview and frame images.
a11y: Handles are labelled sliders with keyboard steps, but playback and transitions ignore reduced-motion. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark rounded card holding a wide mountain preview in a rounded frame, with a timestamp pill and a round play button on it. Beneath sits a thin filmstrip crossed by two orange handles, a small ruler labelled in seconds, and a kept-length line.
behaves: Dragging a handle narrows or widens the kept range, snapping to whole seconds and dimming the trimmed footage; dragging between the handles slides the whole clip. The playhead loops inside the selection, and Reset restores the full length.
customise: Props set the preview image and alt text, clip duration, starting range, minimum length and a range-change callback; the filmstrip frame count and colours stay fixed.
weight: light: One image and ten thumbnails; a frame loop runs only while playback is on.
demo: A panoramic photo of snowy mountain peaks above a sea of clouds, 12 seconds long.
issues: The filmstrip and preview use one still panorama, so every frame looks alike.
polishWhy: Convincing, tactile trimmer with snapping and a tidy ruler; the preview is a static stand-in.
